description: Step 3 of fz-sc8.192 (page v2). lib/map.fz iterates by entry index. User approved the fz-sc8.192.3 page (https://claude.ai/artifact/F9TAVAGpsR1YNK5nGbVYTC, From: Optimize; relayed 2026-11-20): instead of a cursor, a walk is a one-pass list, as in Elixir (Enumerable.reduce for a map is List.reduce(:maps.to_list(map)); member? is a single match). Three one-pass runtime entries, fz_map_to_list, fz_map_keys and fz_map_values, copy the stored (word, kind) pairs straight into list cells and tuples; lib/map.fz follows Elixir's shape. Removes fz_map_entry_key, fz_map_entry_value, map_entry_refs_at, map_view_entry_refs and the index loops. Baseline (bench, develop ec0ca8a8a, instructions per entry over 100,000 keys, fz vs BEAM): Map.to_list 2,417/141, Map.keys 1,138/88, Enum.reduce over the map 2,011/185, over a list of the same pairs 757/44. Owner: Optimize.

comments.text: Measured 2026-11-14 on develop 37a5ef63b (debug, opt-level 1), 100,000 integer keys, ten walks: Enum.reduce over the map 290 ns per entry, Map.to_list the same, Enum.reduce over a list of the same pairs 60 ns per entry. The walk by entry index costs about 230 ns per entry more than a list walk. Probe: scratchpad ovf/w.exs.

title: A walk over a large map does not pay per entry to find its place
